hints: Focus on writing the balanced equation first for one mole of hydrogen forming gaseous water, and notice how much oxygen that really needs.
List the bonds broken as one $\text{H-H}$ plus half an $\text{O=O}$, and the bonds made as two $\text{O-H}$ in one $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Apply $\Delta H$ = energy in to break bonds minus energy out to make bonds, remembering that forming bonds releases energy.
walkthrough:
**Write the equation for one mole of hydrogen**

Think of what actually reacts. One mole of hydrogen makes one mole of water vapour.

$$\text{H}_2(g) + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$$

**Count bonds broken and bonds made**

Breaking needs energy in, making releases energy out. Be careful with the half mole of oxygen and the two O-H bonds in water.

$$\text{Broken} = 1 \times E(\text{H-H}) + \tfrac{1}{2} \times E(\text{O=O})$$

**Put in the numbers and calculate**

Now do the arithmetic calmly. Broken is positive, made is subtracted.

$$\text{Broken} = 436 + \tfrac{1}{2}(496) = 436 + 248 = 684 \text{ kJ}$$

**Finish with bonds made**

One water molecule has two O-H bonds, so double the O-H energy.

$$\text{Made} = 2 \times 463 = 926 \text{ kJ}$$
$$\Delta H = \text{broken} - \text{made} = 684 - 926 = -242 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

options.A: Incorrect. This comes from counting only one $\text{O-H}$ bond made: $684 - 463 = +221$. Remember one $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains two $\text{O-H}$ bonds, so you must use $2 \times 463$.
options.B: Incorrect. This comes from using a whole $\text{O}_2$ molecule for one $\text{H}_2$: $436 + 496 - 926 = +6$. The balanced equation for one mole of $\text{H}_2$ needs only $\tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$, so halve the $\text{O=O}$ energy.
options.C: Correct. Well done. Bonds broken = $436 + 248 = 684$ kJ, bonds made = $926$ kJ, so $\Delta H = 684 - 926 = -242$ kJ per mole of $\text{H}_2$. The negative sign shows combustion to form water is exothermic.
options.D: Incorrect. This comes from using the $\text{O-O}$ single bond energy (146) instead of the $\text{O=O}$ double bond energy (496): $436 + 73 - 926 = -417$. Oxygen as a reactant is $\text{O}_2$ with a double bond.
